title: Hitting a Moving Target: Test-Time Adaptation for AI Text Detection under Continual Distribution Shift
abstract: arXiv:2606.25152v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Deployed AI text detection approaches are supervised, relying on training-time access to labeled datasets of both human-written and AI-generated text. This approach is vulnerable to three types of distribution shifts that occur continually post-deployment, and for which labeled data is often unavailable: adversarial humanization, new LLMs being released, and unidentifiable temporal drift in human writing after widespread LLM usage. Simultaneously, existing approaches do not leverage a key signal of LLM usage: inference-time homogeneity. We propose a test-time adaptation (TTA) approach that adapts to distribution shifts by leveraging homogeneity among unlabeled samples observed at inference time. translated_title: 命中移动目标：持续分布偏移下AI文本检测的测试时自适应方法
translated_abstract: 已部署的AI文本检测方法是监督式的，依赖于训练时能够获取人工撰写和AI生成文本的带标签数据集。这种方法容易受到三类部署后持续发生的分布偏移的影响，而针对这些偏移往往没有带标签数据可用：对抗性人味化处理、新的大语言模型（LLM）的发布，以及LLM广泛使用后人类写作中难以识别的时间漂移。同时，现有方法没有利用LLM使用的一个关键信号：推理时的同质性。我们提出了一种测试时自适应（TTA）方法，通过利用推理时观察到的无标签样本之间的同质性来适应分布偏移。实证研究表明，最先进的监督式检测器在遭遇AI生成文本和人类写作的分布偏移时——无论是对抗性的还是自然发生的——都会系统性地失败，而结合半监督学习的TTA方法则具有较强的鲁棒性。（注：摘要原文此处被截断）
tldr: 该论文提出一种测试时自适应（TTA）方法，利用推理时无标签样本间的同质性，使AI文本检测器能够持续应对对抗性人味化、新LLM发布及人类写作时间漂移等分布偏移问题。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a test-time adaptation approach that leverages inference-time homogeneity among unlabeled samples to enable AI text detectors to remain robust under continual distribution shifts, including adversarial humanization, new LLM releases, and temporal drift in human writing.
